facts.raw_span: 2-week history of vegetating, bleeding plaques and pustules on his face, scalp, trunk, and extremities
Lesions began as pustules and developed into painful, itchy plaques
Pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques were seen on the scalp, legs, arms, and trunk along with keloidal plaques on the face
difficulty walking due to skin lesions
Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay testing for HIV was negative
Punch biopsy from arm showed: Epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils
Dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration
Microabscesses scattered with eosinophils
No granulomas or multinucleated giant cells
Negative periodic acid–Schiff staining
Extensive vegetative plaques with bleeding and ulceration
Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia (hematoxylin-eosin stain)

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia, dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, and microabscesses, is consistent with Pyoderma Gangrenosum.
The patient's symptoms of fever, leukocytosis, and tender, erythematous skin lesions, along with the histopathological findings, are consistent with Sweet Syndrome.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the negative HIV test and lack of granulomas or multinucleated giant cells, could be consistent with Eczema Herpeticum, although the absence of a clear herpetic rash makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, could be consistent with Psoriasis, although the presence of microabscesses and the patient's age make this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the histopathological findings of microabscesses and the lack of granulomas or multinucleated giant cells, could be consistent with Dermatitis Herpetiformis, although the absence of a clear intestinal disease makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia, dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, and microabscesses, is consistent with Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, could be consistent with Autoimmune Bullous Dermatosis, although the absence of a clear blistering rash makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the negative HIV test and lack of granulomas or multinucleated giant cells, could be consistent with Infectious Eczematoid Dermatitis, although the absence of a clear infectious agent makes this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, could be consistent with Seborrheic Dermatitis, although the presence of microabscesses and the patient's age make this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's symptoms of painful, itchy plaques, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, could be consistent with Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris, although the absence of a clear palmoplantar keratoderma makes this diagnosis less likely.
The presence of pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques, along with the negative HIV test and negative periodic acid-Schiff staining, points towards Pustular Psoriasis.
